intro: DWG to DXF converts AutoCAD DWG drawings to DXF, the exchange format opened by LibreCAD, QCAD, FreeCAD, Inkscape, laser cutters and almost every CAD and CAM program, without having AutoCAD.

The conversion is done by LibreDWG, GNU's free DWG library, and it accepts drawings saved with AutoCAD R13, R14, 2000, 2004, 2007, 2010, 2013 and 2018. Its quality is uneven: lines, arcs, circles, polylines, text and layers usually come through well, but some AutoCAD-specific entities, such as complex hatches, associative dimensions or vertical application objects, may be missing or change. The result note reminds you.

Before you get the DXF it is checked to open and audited with ezdxf, so you will not receive a broken file. LibreDWG runs in an isolated environment that only sees your drawing, with bounded time and memory.

You can convert up to five drawings per task and download them together in a ZIP. If you want to view or print it, use DWG to PDF. Files are processed on our server in the European Union and deleted automatically when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more DWG files.
Download the DXF or the ZIP with all of them.

faq.q: Why is something missing in the DXF?
faq.a: Because LibreDWG does not yet translate every AutoCAD entity. If it matters, open it in a program that shows it fully and export it from there.
R13 to 2018. Older DWG files (R12 and earlier) cannot be read.
Yes, with their names and colours, like blocks and text.

faq.q: Which DXF version does it write?
faq.a: LibreDWG writes a DXF that AutoCAD, LibreCAD, QCAD and FreeCAD read; if your CAM program needs an older version, open it in LibreCAD and save it again.
